answer: An agent economy can triangulate each identity's physical network position: several independent beacon nodes issue simultaneous latency challenges, and only a machine truly at one location can answer all of them within the tight round-trip bounds. A Sybil operator's identities all triangulate back to the same island of hardware, no matter how many names they invent - like water vanishing into karst, the extra identities leave no separate physical trace. One location can bridge only one identity, so each fake costs a whole new machine in a new place.
